passage:
By lunchtime the hostel common room had gone quiet whenever Nazia walked in. Everyone knew that Arif had been seeing someone else; someone had leaked a screenshot into the floor group chat, and the replies were piling up: angry stickers, opinions, jokes.

Bidisha, her friend from the next room, slid over a phone. "Post the whole thing. Everyone should see what he did. I'll tag him."

Nazia's throat was tight. She wanted him to hurt, but the idea of her worst week living on strangers' screens made her feel sick. "No. I'm not doing that to him or to me."

She left the room. That evening she sat on her bed with Bidisha and one other friend, Sunita, and cried until her ribs ached. It was small, and it was hers.

qa.q: What had someone leaked into the floor group chat?
qa.a: Someone had leaked a screenshot showing that Arif had been seeing someone else.

qa.q: Why did Nazia refuse Bidisha's suggestion to post everything?
qa.a: She wanted Arif to hurt, but she felt sick at the thought of her worst week living on strangers' screens, so she chose to keep her pain private.

qa.q: What did Nazia do after leaving the common room that helped her?
qa.a: She sat with two trusted friends, Bidisha and Sunita, and let herself cry, keeping her pain among a few listeners.

qa.q: How might Bidisha see Nazia's refusal to post?
qa.a: Bidisha meant to stand up for her friend and may have felt anger for her, and could see later that Nazia was protecting herself.

grounding: Shows public shaming after cheating in a shared institution, with the person keeping the pain private and leaning on a few trusted friends.

passage: By Tuesday the whole hostel seemed to know that Ritu's boyfriend had cheated. In the mess, girls she barely knew stopped her: 'We should post his chats, everyone should see what he is.' Someone had already made a meme with his photo, and it was circulating in the batch group. Ritu felt humiliated, as if her pain had become a show. She pushed her plate away and went back to her room. Ishita, her roommate, knocked a few minutes later. 'Do you want me to shut this down?' Ritu nodded, tears finally falling. Ishita messaged the batch group: 'Please delete the meme. This is Ritu's private pain, not entertainment.' Then she sat on the floor with her. Ritu said, 'I'm so angry at him. But I don't want to humiliate him online. That's not who I am.' 'Then don't. Tell me instead. And your sister. That's enough people.' That night Ritu turned off her notifications and called her sister.

qa.q: What had someone made with the boyfriend's photo?
qa.a: A meme, circulating in the batch group.

qa.q: How did Ritu feel when strangers in the mess stopped her?
qa.a: She felt humiliated, as if her pain had become a show.

qa.q: What did Ritu and Ishita do to keep the pain private?
qa.a: Ishita asked the group to delete the meme, and Ritu chose not to post anything, confiding only in Ishita and her sister.

qa.q: How does Ishita see the hostel's reaction?
qa.a: As turning Ritu's private pain into entertainment, which she asks them to stop.

grounding: Shows a young woman whose partner's cheating becomes public gossip, keeping her pain private, refusing to humiliate him online and leaning on a few trusted people.

passage:
Dear Zubin,
I know you posted those screenshots of Anika's messages because you were angry on my behalf. I know you meant it as loyalty. Thank you for caring that much.
But please take the post down today.
I've been reading the comments, and they make me feel worse, not better. People I don't even know are calling her names, and some are asking me for 'the full story'. My hurt has turned into something everyone can watch. I didn't want that. What she did broke something in me, and I'm still angry. But humiliating her in public doesn't undo it, and I don't want to become someone who uses his pain as a weapon.
What would help is exactly what you did on Sunday night, before the post: sitting in my room with bad tea and letting me talk. I need a few people who'll listen, not a crowd.
Can you come over tomorrow?
Siddharth

qa.q: How do the post and its comments make Siddharth feel?
qa.a: Worse, not better; he feels humiliated that his hurt has become something everyone can watch.

qa.q: What does Siddharth ask for instead of public exposure?
qa.a: That Zubin delete the post and simply listen, as on Sunday night, as one of a few trusted listeners.

qa.q: Why did Zubin post the screenshots?
qa.a: Out of anger and loyalty on Siddharth's behalf, meaning to protect him.

grounding: A letter from a young man hurt by a partner's cheating, asking a friend to remove a public exposure and seeking a few trusted listeners instead.
